answer: The economy samples grading quorums only from established identities that stake reputation (their ridge of accumulated standing) on each verdict. New threads of activity must earn entry before an agent can grade. An attacker spawning fake comet-like identities gets no sampling weight until they build real history, so each sybil costs months of honest participation plus capital locked at stake; a bad quorum verdict slashes that stake across every linked identity, making fake-identity farming costlier than honest work.
